newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore gas oil firms on tight Sept supplies.
newsitem.headline: Singapore gas oil firms on tight Sept supplies.

text.p: Singapore gas oil continued to strengthen further on talks of tight September supplies, industry sources said on Monday.
Trading sources said that South Korea had sold out all its September barrels with the last 30,000 tonne cargo done on Friday at about $27.00 fob Korea.
A trader was bidding 200,000 barrels for Sept 24-28 lifting at 27.50 with no firm sellers seen against it, traders said.
Jet remains under pressure on ample stocks in the region with most buyers covered for their September and October demand, traders said.

A trader offered October 5-9 lifting jet fuel at $29.00 fob Singapore. The jet/gas oil spread has narrowed due to rising gas oil prices and a softening jet market. India bought five October kerosene cargoes totalling 210,000 tonnes in its tender.

Light distillates firmed with crude but the region was still assessed well-supplied. India sold 25,000 tonnes of low aromatic naphtha for September 22-24 lifting from Bombay to Brazilian state-owned Petrobras at $14 per tonne below Northwest European quotes fob basis, industry sources said. Indian cargoes were heading west due to lower north Asian demand in October when petrochemical plants undergo autumn shutdowns.

A Chinese refiner has small cargoes of 93-octane unleaded gasoline lifting in September as well as full 20,000 tonne-cargoes in October but indicated neither a fixed nor floating selling idea due to the market thiness.
In Singapore, an offer was heard for 50,000 barrels of 95-octane unleaded since early morning at $22.45 a barrel lifting September 24-28.

High sulphur fuel oil firmed on large September imports by India which bought a total of 100,000 tonnes. A major was heard bidding for 180 cst cargoes loading in September and October at $114-$115 per tonne. --Singapore Newsroom (+65-8703093)
